confirmed.title: CTE-alias shadowing skips ALL object/schema authorization for schema-qualified tables
confirmed.description: _walk_validate collects every CTE alias in the statement (lines 215-217), then for each exp.Table node does `if name.lower() in cte_aliases: continue` (line 247), comparing only the BARE table name and ignoring whether the reference is schema/catalog-qualified. In SQL a schema-qualified name (e.g. hr.salaries) can NEVER refer to a CTE — CTEs are matched only by unqualified name — so the engine reads the real table while the guard skips check_object() and the default-deny resolver entirely (lines 249-252 are never reached). This defeats BOTH the schema allowlist and the object default-deny at once, for any dialect that supports CTEs (postgres, mysql, tsql, oracle, clickhouse). No name collision with a real permitted object is needed; the attacker just picks a CTE alias equal to the target table's unqualified name.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Connection restricts allowed_schemas=[reporting] with default_deny_objects=True. `SELECT * FROM hr.salaries` is correctly DENIED (schema 'hr' not permitted). But `WITH salaries AS (SELECT 1) SELECT * FROM hr.salaries` is ALLOWED — verified against the real SqlGuard: returns kind='select' with ZERO check_object calls and an empty referenced-tables list. Postgres/MySQL/etc. execute the raw string (server.py:846 -> connector executes spec.sql) and read the forbidden hr.salaries. Equivalent: `WITH secret AS (SELECT 1) SELECT * FROM secret_schema.secret` reads any schema-qualified object the DB login can access.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Only skip the check for UNqualified references, which are the only ones that can bind to a CTE: replace line 247 with `if node.db is None and node.catalog is None and name.lower() in cte_aliases: continue`. A schema- or catalog-qualified table must always fall through to _check_ref.

confirmed.title: Object resolver is not schema-scoped: unqualified name resolves against tables in forbidden schemas
confirmed.description: guard_for() builds the default-deny resolver from app.tables_for(policy, connector), which calls list_tables(None, kinds, None) (server.py:124) — i.e. tables across ALL schemas (postgres list_tables only excludes pg_catalog/information_schema, it does NOT filter by allowed_schemas). _LiveResolver then builds its unqualified name set from that full cross-schema list (server.py:137). For an unqualified table reference, _check_ref returns early from check_object (schema is None) and authorizes solely on resolver.resolve(None, name) = name in _names (sql_guard.py:263-270 / server.py:141-142). So an unqualified name that exists only in a NON-allowed schema resolves True and is permitted. confirmed.title: Postgres EXPLAIN with parenthesized options is entirely rejected (breaks the standard EXPLAIN syntax)
confirmed.description: The postgres/clickhouse EXPLAIN branch matches only `^EXPLAIN\s+(ANALYZE\s+)?(.+)$` (line 296). PostgreSQL's standard and recommended option syntax uses parentheses — `EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON) SELECT ...`, `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) SELECT ...`, `EXPLAIN (VERBOSE) SELECT ...`. For these, group(1) is None (the paren form is not the bare `ANALYZE ` keyword), so `(.+)` becomes `(FORMAT JSON) SELECT ...`, which _parse_single then fails to parse and denies. Every parenthesized-option EXPLAIN is rejected. It fails closed (safe, not a bypass), but db_explain is unusable for the normal postgres option form, which is a broken realistic path.

confirmed.title: A query waiting on _exec_lock that hits its deadline cancels the *other* caller's running query
confirmed.description: execute_query serializes on `_exec_lock` (postgres l.331, sqlite l.475, oracle l.333, clickhouse l.254) and `_execute` records the running connection in a single slot (`_cancel_target` / `_current_conn`). The executor (services/executor.py l.87-99) calls `connector.cancel_current()` when *any* call's deadline fires, including a call that is still blocked waiting for the lock. cancel_current reads the slot, which belongs to the query that is actually running for a different caller, and cancels it (psycopg conn.cancel(), sqlite interrupt(), oracledb cancel()). The waiter then gets TIMEOUT, the innocent running query fails with QueryCanceled/'interrupted', and the connector is poisoned for everyone.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Query A (45 s scan, timeout 60 s) is running on connection 'finance'. Query B arrives with the default 30 s timeout and blocks on _exec_lock. Alternatively acquire `_exec_lock` with `acquire(timeout=remaining)` and raise a LIMIT error on contention so a waiter can never reach the executor deadline while another query holds the lock.

gaps.area: Audit log and metadata-cache files are created world-readable (no chmod in code, no UMask= in the systemd unit)
gaps.why_it_matters: P2 — Verified by execution: with a default 022 umask, AuditLog.record (src/universal_db_mcp/services/audit.py:59) creates audit.jsonl with mode 0644; there is no chmod/umask/0o600 anywhere in src/ (grep confirmed zero hits), and packaging/systemd/universal-db-mcp.service sets no UMask=. Suggested fix: add UMask=0077 to [Service] in packaging/systemd/universal-db-mcp.service, and/or have AuditLog/MetadataCache enforce 0o600 on the created file (os.fchmod on the open handle).

critic.summary: The uncovered surface is mostly deployment/packaging hygiene rather than new protocol-layer holes. Verified by execution: (1) AuditLog creates its file 0644 under a default umask (reproduced: mode 0o644) and the systemd unit sets no UMask, so the audit trail — which can contain raw SQL text (next finding) — is world-readable in the shipped deployment; (2) server.py appends audit sql_text AFTER redact_value, so with audit_sql_text=true literal credentials inside query text bypass the redaction chokepoint that redact.py's own docstring declares absolute; (3) the built wheel in the bundle declares oracledb<4 while the wheelhouse ships oracledb 4.0.2, so installing the package with its [oracle] extra from the bundle cannot resolve; (4) scripts/fixtures/start_mock_dbs.sh uses $((++tries)) under set -u and dies with 'tries: unbound variable' (exit 127) on exactly the Db2 bootstrap-failure path its comment anticipates. Also concrete but not executed: the air-gap baseline image is built from a floating ubuntu:24.04 tag with no digest pin, doctor reports a config with no audit_path as healthy, HTTP-mode 'caller-scoped' history/cursors key on the server OS user (identical for all bearer clients), the Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK hardcodes port 8765 against a configurable http_port, and the docs/SBOM claim a vulnerability scan is re-run per release while no scan tooling or CI exists anywhere in the repo. Areas I checked and found clean: SQL input size (sql_guard enforces a 64 KiB _MAX_SQL_BYTES limit, so the oversized-SQL DoS I suspected does not exist), pagination cursors (stateless HMAC tokens with TTL and identity/policy binding — no server-side state to exhaust), audit rotation/fail-closed logic (locked, fsynced, shielded write), compose hardening (read-only rootfs, no-new-privileges, pull_policy: never, loopback-only port), mock-database seeds (clearly fictional themed data, loopback-only ports, secret files 0600), and prompt-injection via database content (view/routine definitions and rows reach the model unmarked, but no doc claims otherwise and masking warnings already label the heuristic controls, so there is no concrete defect to file against the documented behavior).
